lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Choose + or − and solve: "Sam had 520 stickers and gave 185 to friends. How many are left?"

FEEDBACK
Subtraction: 520−185=335 left.

WATCH FOR
Picking an operation from a keyword alone without reading the whole story can choose the wrong action.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Solve eight word problems (four + and four −, mixed 2- and 3-digit). For each: underline the question, choose operation, show working and write one reason sentence.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
A library has 428 books and gets 175 more. That is addition: 428+175=603. The bar grows. If 90 are borrowed from 603, subtract to find what remains.

TRY FIRST
Choose + or − and solve: "Sam had 520 stickers and gave 185 to friends. How many are left?"

FEEDBACK
Subtraction: 520−185=335 left.
teach_steps.explain:
Addition and subtraction word problems need a chosen operation, a model (bar or place working) and a reason that matches the story.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Picking an operation from a keyword alone without reading the whole story can choose the wrong action. Correct the value or method, not just the appearance of the digits.
